segments: The Chronography of Bar Hebraeus.
Sa'd al-Din the eunuch,
he who had been left by Nur al-Din as governor of the fortress of Mosul,
fled from Sayf al-Din and came to the son of his master.
Now the Damascenes, since they were afraid of Saladin,
sent and sought peace from Amalric, king of Jerusalem,
and they took upon themselves tribute.
And after a few days, that king became sick,
and he died in Acre on the eleventh {OCR?} of the month of Tammuz,
forty days after the death of Nur al-Din.
And there was great mourning among the Christians at the death of this victorious king,
for fear of him had fallen upon all the Arabs of Egypt and of Syria.
And in his place arose Baldwin the Fourth {OCR?}, his son.
And Kilij Arslan, the Sultan of Iconium, also, when he heard that Nur al-Din had died, who had been the helper of Dhu'l-Nun the son of Danishmand,
entered their lands,
and took control over Sebastia, Neocaesarea, and Comana.
And Dhu'l-Nun himself fled to Constantinople,
and took refuge with the king of the Greeks.
And here came to an end their rule,
after they had ruled for 122 {years}.
[... and the] Emir of Maypherqat,
they sent {OCR?} to Shah-Arman, lord of Khilat,
and he surrendered (or they surrendered? {OCR?}) to him all their fortresses.
And the king of the Iberians again turned and took the city of Ani from the Persians.
And in the year one thousand four hundred and eighty-five of the Greeks,
570 of the Arabs,
Saladin gathered his forces,
and came from Egypt to Damascus,
showing as if he had come for the aid of the son of his master,
and he entered and lodged in his father's house.
And secretly he bribed Rayhan the eunuch, the governor of the fortress,
and he opened the gate to him.
And Saladin brought Sayf al-Islam his brother and his men into the fortress of Damascus,
and gained control over it, without abolishing the proclamation {khutbah} of al-Malik al-Salih Ismail.
And he went out from Damascus and came against Homs and took it.
And from there he came to Hamath and gained control over it.
And he came and encamped upon the mountain called Jawshan, which is beside Aleppo. Now the emirs who were in it
set up heralds and assembled all the people of Aleppo, great and small, in the hippodrome of the Iraq Gate,
